details.description: text-embedding-ada-002-v2 is version 2 of OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002 model, which converts text into a 1,536-dimension numerical vector for measuring semantic relatedness between pieces of text. Microsoft's Azure OpenAI documentation distinguishes this version from version 1 of the same model by its larger 8,192-token maximum request size, versus 2,046 tokens for version 1. OpenAI's own model documentation labels the underlying text-embedding-ada-002 model an "Older embedding model," superseded by the third-generation text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large models.
advantages: Accepts requests of up to 8,192 tokens, versus 2,046 tokens for version 1 of the same model, per Microsoft's Azure OpenAI documentation.
Produces 1,536-dimension text embeddings usable with the Embeddings API, per OpenAI's model documentation and Microsoft's Azure OpenAI documentation.
Microsoft's Azure OpenAI documentation notes there is no in-place upgrade path between embedding models; moving to a newer model such as text-embedding-3-large requires regenerating embeddings.
disadvantages: OpenAI's own model page labels the underlying text-embedding-ada-002 model an "Older embedding model."
Scores lower on both MTEB (61.0 vs. 62.3/64.6) and MIRACL (31.4 vs. 44.0/54.9) than text-embedding-3-small/large, per OpenAI's reported testing as published in Microsoft's Azure OpenAI documentation.
Can only be used with Embedding API requests, not chat completions or other endpoints, per OpenAI's model documentation.

notes: This target's slug and providers (["openai"]) point to the plain OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 model. OpenAI's own current docs and API reference do not use the literal string 'text-embedding-ada-002-v2' anywhere I could open, but Microsoft's Azure OpenAI documentation explicitly documents 'text-embedding-ada-002 (version 2)' as a distinct row with an 8,192-token max request, versus 2,046 tokens for '(version 1)' -- matching the catalog's max_input_tokens of 8191 (off by one from Azure's 8,192, as also seen for the plain text-embedding-ada-002 target). I treated this target as that version-2 designation of the same underlying model and did not state a token limit beyond what the catalog already provides. No specific supported-language list or release date was found on an opened page.
